fixes.row: Truth beside justice, righteousness, judgment and peace
fixes.why: Rule 6: the third shown example, Ps 85:10, prints 'faithfulness', not 'truth' (and says nothing of justice or judgment); about eight verses in the row show 'faithfully', 'faithfulness' or 'true reward' where the label says 'Truth'.
fixes.fix: Relabel 'Truth or faithfulness beside justice, righteousness, judgment and peace'; change lead to Jer.4.2, Zech.8.16, Ps.111.7, Eph.5.9 (all print 'truth' or 'true' beside justice or righteousness).

fixes.row: Truth beside justice, righteousness, judgment and peace
fixes.why: Rule 4: Hebrew אֱמֶת and Greek ἀλήθεια sit in one row under 'Truth'. The row's note ('the first build kept them in two rows') is build history, not something a reader can use, and it never says the two words are different. The reader is told only in row 1.
fixes.fix: Replace the note with: 'Two different words: Hebrew אֱמֶת (the Berean prints it "truth", "faithfulness" or "true") and Greek ἀλήθεια; each example names its word.'

fixes.why: Rules 4 and 6: the fourth shown example, Gen 24:27, prints 'kindness and faithfulness', so the label's 'Loving devotion' is not shown in it (four more verses print 'kindness'). Separately, the Berean also prints a different Hebrew word, אֱמוּנָה, 'faithfulness' in many verses that are not in this hub, so a reader may take these 41 'faithfulness' verses for all of English 'faithfulness'.
fixes.fix: Change lead to Ps.85.10, Exod.34.6, Prov.3.3, Ps.86.15. Extend the note: 'The Berean prints חֶסֶד "loving devotion", "kindness" or "mercy". Another Hebrew word, אֱמוּנָה, is also printed "faithfulness"; it is not in this hub.'

fixes.row: The word of truth, “Your word is truth”, the truth of the gospel
fixes.why: Rules 1 and 5: nine Hebrew Scripture verses sit under a label ending 'the truth of the gospel' and a note that readers take 'the word' of Scripture, Christ or the gospel. Four of them are not God's word at all: Joseph testing his brothers' words (Gen 42:16), the Queen of Sheba's report of Solomon (1 Kgs 10:6, 2 Chr 9:5), Mordecai's letters (Esth 9:30). Filing them here reads human speech as 'the word of truth' and frames the Hebrew Scriptures through the NT phrase.
fixes.fix: Move Gen.42.16, 1Kgs.10.6, 2Chr.9.5, Esth.9.30 to 'Every other use' (or a row 'Words said to be true'). Keep God's word verses (Ps 119:43, 119:160, 2 Sam 7:28, 1 Kgs 17:24, Jer 23:28, Dan 10:1) but lead with Ps.119.160, John.17.17, Eph.1.13, Gal.2.5, and scope the note to the NT verses: 'In the New Testament phrases (Eph 1:13, Col 1:5, Jas 1:18, John 17:17), readers take "the word" of Scripture, of Christ or of the gospel; the page does not choose.'

fixes.why: Titus 1:14 ('Jewish myths or the commands of men who have rejected the truth') is filed in a row of 'Truth and the law, commandments' beside Neh 9:13, Ps 119:142 and Mal 2:6. The verse speaks of men's commands and myths, not of God's law, but placed here it reads as if Torah and commandments stand against the truth, and a rabbi will see the row's heading do that work.
fixes.fix: Remove Titus.1.14 from this row (it stays in 'Against the truth', where its own words place it).

fixes.why: Rule 5: seven of twelve verses are the Hebrew Scriptures speaking of their own law ('Your law is true', 'true laws'), yet the example order shown is 2 Chr 15:3 then three NT verses, and the whole row carries the note 'Christian traditions part on the law and the gospel'. The Torah's own claim is heard second and through a Christian dispute.
fixes.fix: Lead with Ps.119.142, Neh.9.13, Mal.2.6, John.1.17. Scope the note to the NT verses: 'In John 1:17, Rom 2:20 and similar New Testament verses, Christian traditions part on the law and the gospel; the page takes no side.'

fixes.row: Against the truth: the lie, wickedness, deception, turning from it; truth missing
fixes.why: Rule 1: the label says 'Against the truth', but about eight verses affirm truth set beside the lie (Prov 12:19 'Truthful lips endure', Rom 9:1 'I speak the truth ... I am not lying', 1 Tim 2:7, Prov 14:25, 1 Cor 13:6 'rejoices in the truth'). Prov 12:19 and Eph 4:25 are shown examples. A label that says 'against' over verses that are for the truth says more than they do.
fixes.fix: Relabel 'Truth and its opposites: the lie, wickedness, deception; turning from it; truth missing'.

fixes.row: Truth said of Christ, of Jesus
fixes.why: Rom 9:1 is Paul's oath ('I speak the truth in Christ; I am not lying'): the truth is Paul's speech, not something said of Christ. The label is a claim about Christ, and a by-hand row on the divine persons should hold only verses that say it.
fixes.fix: Move Rom.9.1 out of this row (it already stands in 'Speak the truth ...'). If a looser row is wanted, relabel the remaining six 'Truth and Christ, Jesus'.

fixes.why: Rule 4: two different Greek words are in one row under 'true': ἀληθής ('truthful', John 3:33, Rom 3:4) and ἀληθινός ('true, genuine', as against idols, John 17:3, 1 Thess 1:9, Rev 6:10). 'God is true' reads as one claim; 'the only true God' and 'the living and true God' say genuine as against other gods. Only the first adjective row carries the two-words note, and the Testimony row has the same mix.
fixes.fix: Add a note to 'God is true' and to the Testimony row: 'Two Greek words are printed "true": ἀληθής (truthful) and ἀληθινός (genuine, real). Each example names its word.' Optionally relabel 'God is true; the only true God, the true God'.

fixes.row: Testimony, words and judgments called true; “faithful and true”
fixes.why: Rules 1 and 6: the fourth shown example, Rev 15:3, calls God's 'ways' true, which the label omits (it lists testimony, words, judgments). Six John verses print 'valid' / 'not valid', not 'true'; the note names only John 5:31.
fixes.fix: Relabel 'Testimony, words, ways and judgments called true; "faithful and true"'. Extend the note: 'The Berean prints the same Greek word "valid" in John 5:31-32, 8:13-14, 8:17.'

fixes.row: Knowing the truth: knowledge, wisdom, instruction
fixes.why: Rule 2: the note names only whom God wills to save and how one is brought to the knowledge. Heb 10:26 ('after we have received the knowledge of the truth' ... 'no further sacrifice') is the text on which Reformed, Wesleyan and Baptist readers part over whether it can be lost, and it is not named. The note also sits over four Hebrew Scripture verses that have nothing to do with it.
fixes.fix: Rewrite: 'In the New Testament phrase "the knowledge of the truth" (1 Tim 2:4, 2 Tim 2:25, Heb 10:26, Titus 1:1), Christian traditions part on whom God wills to save, how one comes to it, and whether it can be lost; the page takes no side.'

fixes.row: Truth beside faith, obedience and love
fixes.why: Rule 2: 2 Thess 2:13 ('God chose you from the beginning to be saved ... by faith in the truth') and 2:10 ('the love of the truth that would have saved them') are the election and free-will texts, not named in the note; the note also covers the Hebrew Zech 8:19 and Isa 61:8 as 'Christian' matters.
fixes.fix: Rewrite the note, scoped: 'In the New Testament verses, Christian traditions part on what faith is, how it is given, how God's choosing stands to it, and how it stands to obedience and love; the page takes no side.'

fixes.row: Set free, sanctified, purified, guided by the truth
fixes.why: Rule 2: this row has no note, but 'purified your souls by obedience to the truth' and 'sanctify them by the truth' are where the traditions part on sanctification, obedience and purification (the worker flagged this as contested point 7). Every neighbouring row of this kind carries a no-side note.
fixes.fix: Add: 'Where Christian traditions part on how sanctification and purifying come about, and what part obedience has in them, the page takes no side.'

fixes.row: “Your truth,” “Your faithfulness,” said to the LORD, to God
fixes.why: Rule 1: Ps 119:151 ('all Your commandments are true') is neither 'Your truth' nor 'Your faithfulness'; the label is a quotation and this verse does not contain it.
fixes.fix: Remove Ps.119.151 from the pick (it already stands in 'Truth and the law, commandments' and in the justice row).

worker_points.point: 1. 'The Spirit of truth' (John 14:17, 15:26, 16:13, 1 John 4:6) and 1 John 5:6 as a hand pick
worker_points.why: The note takes no side on how the Spirit relates to the Father and the Son, John 15:26 is quoted whole, and no identification is added beyond what the verse says.

worker_points.point: 2. 1 John 5:20 'Him who is true' / 'the true God' held in its own row
worker_points.why: The row names both readings of 'He' and does not file the verse under God or under Jesus. Good practice.

worker_points.point: 3. 'God is true' by hand, with John 17:3 beside Jesus Christ; 'He who sent Me is true'
worker_points.why: The picks are right and no identification is added, but the row mixes ἀληθής and ἀληθινός without saying so (rule 4); see the fix on the 'God is true' row.

worker_points.point: 4. 'Truth said of Christ' (John 14:6 exclusivism, John 1:17 law and truth)
worker_points.why: No gloss on John 14:6 or 1:17 is the right course, and John 1:17 also standing in the law row is fair. Rom 9:1 does not belong (it is Paul's oath), and the fix on that row removes it.

worker_points.point: 5. 'The knowledge of the truth' (election, universalism, apostasy)
worker_points.why: The no-side note exists but omits whether the knowledge can be lost (Heb 10:26) and is not scoped to the NT verses; see the fix.
The note should also name God's choosing and be scoped to the NT verses; 2 Thess 2:13 appearing in this row is correct.

worker_points.point: 7. 'Set free, sanctified, purified, guided' and 1 Pet 1:22
worker_points.why: The label uses the verses' own verbs and is fine; it needs a no-side note on sanctification and obedience.

worker_points.point: 8. 'The word is truth' / 'the word of truth' / 'the truth of the gospel', no note first built, no-side note added
worker_points.why: The note is right in kind but covers Hebrew verses and human words that are not God's word at all; split off the human words and scope the note.

worker_points.point: 9. 'Truth and the law' (Rom 2:20, Titus 1:14 'Jewish myths', John 1:17, 1 John 2:4)
worker_points.why: The worker saw that Titus 1:14 wants a Jewish reader's eye; it should leave this row. The Hebrew Scripture verses also need to be heard first, with the note scoped to the NT.

worker_points.point: 10. John 8:44 in the 'Against the truth' row, no longer a shown example
worker_points.why: The verse is shown whole, as written, saying who is addressed and who is described, and it is no longer a lead example. Keep it out of every lead list. The relabel of the row removes the heading 'Against the truth' from over it.

worker_points.point: 11. 1 Tim 3:15 'pillar and foundation of the truth' left in 'Every other use'
worker_points.why: It is the second shown example of the catch-all, visible, unlabelled and unglossed. A row for it would invite a claim about church authority the verse does not make.

worker_points.point: 12. Dan 8:12 'it flung truth to the ground' in 'Truth missing'
worker_points.why: The row says only what the verse says about truth and does not identify the horn.
Pooling is honest and the row 1 note is good; but row 2's note says nothing of the two words, and row 1 should say that אֱמוּנָה, also printed 'faithfulness', is not here.

worker_points.point: 14. John 5:31 'not true' kept beside John 8:14 'true'; no harmonizing
worker_points.why: Right as it stands. The note should add that the Berean prints 'valid' in five other verses (see the Testimony fix).

worker_points.point: 15. 'Your truth,' 'Your faithfulness' pick of 8 verses that name the LORD or God
worker_points.why: The rule for the pick is right, but Ps 119:151 does not contain the quoted words; remove it.

worker_points.point: Consolidation: Hebrew and Greek companions now share five rows (justice, walk and way, speak and do, knowing, in truth)
worker_points.why: Rule 4 (checked): sharing a row does not equate the words so long as each example shows its word, and every example does name the lemma, so walk and way, speak and do, knowing and 'in truth' are acceptable. The justice row is the weak one: its note is build history and does not say the words differ (fix above), and its label shows neither Hebrew 'faithfulness' nor Greek 'truth' in the same way. Rule 5 (checked): the shared rows list Hebrew Scripture verses with the NT, but none is filed under an NT-only heading, apart from the word-of-truth/gospel row and the law-row note, both fixed above. The 'In truth' row (41) is honest: its note names 'certainly', 'in fact' and 'correctly' (Acts 4:27, Luke 22:59, Mark 12:32), which print no word for truth, and its first four examples show 'in truth' or 'truly'.

missing.what: 2 John 1:2 ('the truth that abides in us and will be with us forever'), ἀλήθεια, is in no row, not even the catch-all, though 2 John 1:1, 3 and 4 are

Genesis 32:10 (Berean; 32:11 in the Hebrew), 'unworthy of all the kindness and faithfulness', is the Jacob verse that pairs חֶסֶד with אֱמֶת, and is absent from the hub (probably a versification gap); it belongs in the first row

summary: The hub is faithful to the text, keeps the divine persons by hand and handles the Spirit of truth and 1 John 5:20 with care; it should ship once fourteen mostly label and note fixes are made. The weak points are the word-of-truth row (human words and Hebrew verses under 'the truth of the gospel'), Titus 1:14 sitting under the law, the 'Against the truth' label over verses that affirm it, the unmarked Hebrew/Greek and two-Greek-adjective pooling, and a few Christian dispute notes placed over Hebrew Scripture verses.
